heading: Prato
review_text_short: Prato is an attractive Italian themed restaurant and bar handily located next door to the Kyneton Farmers Market. It's a great place for a glass of wine and a pizza. Perhaps doesn't quite live up to its fancy exterior and interior but is still worth a visit if you like feeling special.

heading: Little Swallow Cafe
review_text_short: Little Swallow Cafe is the hippest and busiest eatery in Kyneton. We love the old school atmosphere, the modern contemporary menu and positive vibes that only a busy place can provide you with. Patience may be a virtue as it gets very busy here. For a great cafe experience, Little Swallow Cafe is the place to be.

heading: Major Tom's
review_text_short: Industrial hipster grungy vibe in the country. If this is your personality Major Tom's might be right up your alley. More takeaway styled food than gourmet but if you love supporting live music then worth a visit.

heading: Musk Lane Wines
review_text_short: Centrally located in Kyneton Musk Lane Wines is perfect for your favourite bubbly and wine tasting. No need to go for a 15 minute drive you can just walk there! On a bright sunny day this makes for a perfect stop to add to your day.

heading: Sisko Chocolate
review_text_short: The weekend is for indulging, right? Head to Sisko Chocolate treat. Something a bit stylish and pleasurable for the weekend. We love it!

heading: Botanik
review_text_short: Botanik is all about indulgence and retro charm. If you love your spirits then Botanik is a must visit. Even if you don't Botanik is just  a cool spot. Definitely worth visiting even if for just one or should I say more drinks! We love the vibe.

heading: Campaspe Mill Distillery
review_text_short: Campaspe Mill Distillery is easy to recommend. A lovely distinctive venue to transport you back in time coupled with boutique artisan gin, your other favourite alcoholic beverages, an in-house museum and an understated food menu. Definitely add as a must visit on your trip to Kyneton.

heading: Grist Artisan Baker
review_text_short: Grist Artisan Baker has supersized pastries and cakes fitting for a country location. I like the historic building, value for money and a bit of effort put into their artisan historical branding. With a bit of effort they could really emphasise the historic setting with the bakeries interior design. As it is it's a great stop for the value conscious and if you have children and are travelling from Melbourne you'll find the pricing very generous.
